tasks.task: Write the booking confirmation and reminder message set

items.when: When a new booking system goes in and every message must be written and loaded in order
When you need confirmation, reminders, reschedule, waitlist and no-show follow-up as one set
When you want a second plan: one small step per message and the best time to send each
When reminders are ignored and a change of wording or framing may work better than more of them
Before texts go live, to check length, cost and rule flags for each message

tasks.task: Build a plan to cut no-shows and late cancellations

items.when: Before changing anything, to see where no-shows happen with every figure worked out
When you need reminder timing, deposit or card-hold wording and a fair fee rule
When no-shows start at booking: unclear times, no prep note, no easy way to change
Before deposits or fees start, to check them against consumer rules where the business trades

tasks.task: Design a phone menu and write every prompt

items.when: When callers get lost or wait too long and the menu must be cut to what they need
When you want a second wording of the prompts with pacing and pauses marked
When the menu suits the office's departments, not the effort it costs a caller
When you need to hear the prompts spoken before anyone records them
When a prompt is hard to say or follow by ear, to find and fix each line

tasks.task: Write a front-desk answer book and FAQ

items.when: When the answer to a common question is buried in old emails and policy files
When hours, fees, payment, cancellations and what to bring must be in one answer book
When the same answers should also go on the website as an FAQ page
When the answers state service facts, to check each against what the clinic approved

tasks.task: Write an inbound call script for the desk

items.when: When new or temporary staff need a script with transfer and emergency steps
When the desk is a clinic, to compare replies on bills and bookings with privacy checks
When callers are often upset and staff need a way to hear them out before answering
When the script must fit one page a temp can keep beside the phone
When scripted lines sound stiff out loud, to fix the ones that trip

tasks.task: Write greetings, voicemail, after-hours and hold messages

items.when: When open, closed, holiday and busy times each need their own short message
When you want a second version of each greeting written for the ear, with pauses
When many callers speak another language and need the greeting in it too
Before recording, to fix any line that is hard to say in one breath

tasks.task: Write recall and reactivation messages

items.when: When check-ups or vaccinations are due, or clients have not booked for a long time
When texts may work better than email, to try a short flow with consent rules kept
Before sending, to cut each message to one action: book, call or reply
Before a recall text goes to the whole list, to check cost and rule flags
Before recall messages go out, to confirm the booking link works and there are open slots to book

tasks.task: Write booking and cancellation terms in plain words

items.when: When terms are long or scattered and clients are surprised by fees
When you want a clause-by-clause plain version to compare with your own
When a fee line still sounds harsh or legal after the rewrite
Before the terms are published, to check fees and deposits against local consumer rules

tasks.task: Set up a new-client or new-patient intake process and form

items.when: When intake depends on whoever is at the desk and needs written steps
When a clinic has an approved process that must become plain steps with open questions
When the form is long and needs stages, conditional questions and save and resume
When form labels use office words and clients answer the wrong thing
When clients give up on the form, to cut fields and test the shorter flow
When the form collects health details, to find privacy gaps before it goes live

tasks.task: Reply to public reviews without breaching privacy

items.when: When the practice also needs to know when and how to ask for reviews
When a clinic, vet or salon must reply without confirming anyone is a client
When you want a second reply to compare, to be run through the privacy rules after
When replies come in batches and risky ones should be held for the owner

tasks.task: Find no-show patterns in a booking export

items.when: Before any sums, to find duplicate bookings, blank statuses and odd dates in the export
When you have the export and need no-shows by day, time, service and lead time
When you want the attendance table reconciled and the gaps in the evidence listed
When the owner needs the pattern as one point, its proof and the next step

tasks.task: Turn approved aftercare text into a plain client note

items.when: When a clinician or vet wrote the instructions and the client needs a plain version
When the client reads another language and needs the same note in it
Before it is handed over, to catch a dose, date or name written two ways

tasks.task: Write a new-patient or service page with clear next steps

items.when: Before the page, to take the approved facts on fees, hours and what to bring
When the page should end in a booking flow with open times and a prep note
When the page opens with the practice's story, to compare a version that answers first
Before the page is published, to flag promises and claims the rules do not allow
When the page lists services, to check each line against the approved facts
Before the page is written, to confirm the booking link, prices and open slots a visitor will find today
When the page is finished, so a fresh reader in the new patient's seat lists what they would still ask

tasks.task: Check marketing copy for health and results claims

items.when: Before a clinic, vet or beauty business posts a page, ad or social post
When you want each claim sorted as fine, needs proof or cut, with safer wording
When a post cites a study or number, to check it and what context is missing

tasks.task: Reply to an upset client or pet owner

items.when: When a hard message lands, to read its urgency and warning signs first
When the reply must name the feeling, fix what it can and promise nothing false
When a phone call would do better than a message, to plan how to listen first
Before sending, to check the draft's promises, facts and tone

tasks.task: Run the monthly front desk review

items.when: In the first week of each month, to check no-shows, missed calls, reviews and messages
When this month's booking export is in and the pattern needs updating
When admin work is piling up, to find the step that slows the queue
When the month's numbers look odd, to reconcile attendance before reporting

tasks.task: Set up booking messages and the phone line for a new system

items.when: When a new system or location opens, or no-shows and missed calls are out of hand
When the phone side needs its menu, greetings and desk script written
When desk staff need a written procedure for the new system with its edge cases
When hours or the phone number changed, to make the public listings match

tasks.task: Write a recording brief for a voice artist or AI voice

items.when: When the prompts are final and a voice artist needs names, pace and file names
When the voice will be made by a tool and needs tone, pace and character described
When the practice wants the prompts read by a text-to-speech voice

tasks.task: Plan an AI phone or chat assistant for bookings

items.when: Before any build, to write the approved answers the assistant may give
When the assistant needs flows with questions, recovery from mistakes and a handover
When the assistant should answer calls by voice and book through a tool
When the assistant will hear health details, to find privacy gaps first

tasks.task: Hand over referrals and open desk tasks between staff

items.when: When one person leaves the desk and the next must run it from the first hour
When referral paperwork is part-done and you need what was sent, received and booked
When the referral handover must be checked for missing letters and bookings

tasks.task: Answer a client who writes in another language

items.when: Before translating, to settle the answer from the approved answer book
When a message is not in English and you need its meaning and a reply in their language
When a booking or fee line could be misread, to get a second wording to compare
When the message is a complaint, to check the English draft before it is translated

always.when: Before any message that promises a time, a refund or a call back
When a message or script uses clinic or office words a client would not

helpers.when: When the fix is rotas, fees or desk procedures the owner must decide, not wording
When hours, listings and local search pages must be updated to match the desk
When reviews need a standing plan across sites, not one batch of replies
When an AI phone or chat assistant must be built and tested, not only planned
When health privacy, advertising claims or cancellation fees need a rules check
When the new-patient page or booking page must be built on the practice's site

gaps: The library is thin for front desk work: about 50 items fit, and booking, phone and aftercare work rests on the kit
No library item writes booking confirmations, reminders, reschedule, waitlist or no-show follow-up messages
No library item writes deposit, card-hold or late-cancel fee wording, or offers two versions of booking terms to compare
No library item designs a phone menu or writes greetings, voicemail, after-hours and hold messages
No library item writes an inbound call script for a desk; the call scripts in the library are for cold sales calls
No library item writes recall messages for check-ups, vaccinations or lapsed clients
No library item turns a clinician's or vet's aftercare text into a plain note that adds and drops nothing
No library item writes a privacy-safe review reply for a clinic or vet; the review items are written for shops
No library item writes a new-patient or service page, or checks health advertising rules country by country
No library item plans a waitlist or a way to fill cancelled slots, or a text back to missed callers
No library item is written for vets, salons or studios, and no tool guide covers a booking or phone system
No library item checks an emergency script: what staff say and do when a caller describes an urgent problem
